__comment: REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED THIS ROUND: this used to be "parent": "minecraft:item/generated" with a "layer0" texture - that is a NORMAL flat-sprite model, and BakedModel#isCustomRenderer() is FALSE for it, which means vanilla's ItemRenderer never calls a custom BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer at all - it just renders the flat/extruded layer0 texture directly. That's why the item kept showing the old totem_of_undying-derived texture as a golden 3D-extruded blob no matter what PlayerPickerItemRenderer's own code was changed to: the renderer was never being invoked in the first place. The correct parent for a BEWLR-rendered item (same as vanilla's own shield.json/bed jsons/chest jsons/trident.json) is "builtin/entity" - confirmed against vanilla's actual real shield.json source, not guessed. isCustomRenderer() is TRUE for a builtin/entity model, which is what actually makes Item#initializeClient's registered IClientItemExtensions#getCustomRenderer() get called. No layer0/item texture is used or needed any more - PlayerPickerItemRenderer supplies the actual texture (the generic skin, or a picked player's real skin) directly at render time.
